newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia parliament rejects cabinet proposal.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia parliament rejects cabinet proposal.

text.p: Slovenia's parliament on Thursday rejected prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek's new cabinet by an even vote of 45 against 45.
"The vote was 45 against 45. The prime minister has to present a new government line-up in 10 days," parliamentary president Janez Podobnik told the assembly following a secret ballot.

Dronvsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats last month formed a coalition with the ex-communist United List of Social Democrats, the pensioners' party Desus and the Nationalist Party. His government commanded a majority of just one vote.

He received parliament's mandate to form a new government, the country's third since it gained independence from the former Yugoslavia in 1991, in January following an inconclusive general election almost three months ago.

"The result is indecisive and therefore inadequate. I will try to form a government that will have sufficient support within 10 days," a clearly surprised Drnovsek told state television after the vote.

Earlier in the day, the three rightist parties of the "Spring" alliance which together hold 44 seats called on parliament not to support the government, claiming it would not be able to carry out key tasks such as Slovenia's membership in the European Union or a reform of the ailing pension system.
